top.headline: A Kremlin-linked oligarch secretly bankrolled Trump Jr.'s Bahamas wedding
top.blurb: ProPublica reports that Umar Kremlev, a Russian boxing official close to Vladimir Putin, paid roughly $100,000 to rent a private island and $70,000 for fireworks at Donald Trump Jr.'s May wedding in the Bahamas. The payments ran through a Dubai entity tied to Kremlev's International Boxing Association; a Trump Jr. spokesperson didn't dispute them, calling Kremlev a personal friend.

top.headline: DOJ subpoenas ex-CIA chief Brennan in a 'grand conspiracy' probe of Trump's critics
top.blurb: Prosecutors have subpoenaed former CIA Director John Brennan to testify Oct. 15 before a grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida, his lawyer disclosed. The probe examines whether officials who investigated Trump over the past decade, including the Russia inquiry and the Mar-a-Lago documents case, conspired to violate his civil rights; Brennan is separately a target over past congressional testimony.

top.headline: The Kennedy Center says it can't make payroll within weeks — unless Trump's name stays
top.blurb: The Kennedy Center's board warns it can't cover payroll or maintenance contracts within weeks, and says only Trump — its chairman since he installed loyalists on the board last year — can raise the funds to avert bankruptcy. The board argues a lawsuit blocking his name from the building is costing it donors.

top.headline: In Uttarakhand's voter-roll purge, a handful of BJP-linked agents targeted only Muslim names
top.blurb: Newslaundry's investigation found that a small number of BJP-linked booth-level agents filed thousands of objections to strike names from Uttarakhand's electoral rolls during the state's special intensive revision — and that every name targeted was Muslim, with individual objectors' tallies running into the thousands.

top.headline: Houthi fighters push toward Yemen's last government strongholds in Marib and Taiz
top.blurb: Houthi forces are advancing on Marib, the internationally recognised government's last stronghold in the north and home to Yemen's largest oil and gas fields, while government troops counterattack in Taiz. More than 85,000 people have fled their homes since early September, the IOM says, and analysts warn a Houthi capture of Marib could decisively tilt the decade-long war.

top.headline: Sudan's humanitarian pipeline is weeks from collapse, the UN warns
top.blurb: The UN's migration agency warns Sudan's Common Humanitarian Pipeline could reach an 'imminent end' without urgent donor support, as fighting, floods and mass displacement strain relief networks. Roughly 8.6 million people remain internally displaced in a war that aid workers estimate has killed more than 200,000 since 2023.

top.headline: Abhishek Sharma's fifty powers India past Afghanistan in the T20I opener
top.blurb: Abhishek Sharma's half-century set up a seven-wicket win for India over Afghanistan in the first T20I in Delhi, with 38 balls to spare. The result puts India 1-0 up as the two sides continue their short white-ball series.

top.headline: At 60, Star Trek has never gone this long without a show in the works
top.blurb: Star Trek marks its 60th anniversary with no new series or film officially greenlit, an unprecedented gap for the franchise. Strange New Worlds star Anson Mount says the audience is aging, and while a script is reportedly in development at Paramount, nothing has been confirmed.

bengal.headline: Two Trinamools claim to be the real one, as Bengal's Election Commission decides who gets the symbol
bengal.blurb: A breakaway faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee is contesting Mamata Banerjee's TMC for the party's name and symbol ahead of October 6 by-polls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, with the Election Commission now arbitrating the claim.

bengal.headline: Congress stages a Satyagraha in Thakurnagar to court Bengal's Matua vote
bengal.blurb: Congress workers held a Satyagraha in Thakurnagar against political polarisation, part of a push to rebuild ties with the Matua community, a Scheduled Caste refugee-origin group the BJP and TMC have long courted for its bloc vote.

travel.headline: Lonely Planet's 2026 travel list, and exactly when to go
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet pairs its 2026 Best in Travel destinations, from Botswana to Vietnam, with the specific months worth booking each one for.

travel.headline: A single deer's genome could help save the Philippines' rarest species
travel.blurb: Researchers have sequenced the first draft genome of the critically endangered Visayan spotted deer, down to roughly 700 animals on two Philippine islands, offering a genetic road map for captive-breeding efforts.

happy.headline: In 1381, thousands of English commoners marched on London and stormed the Tower
happy.blurb: Sparked by a third poll tax in four years, villagers from Essex marched on London, breached the Tower for the only time in its history, and demanded the abolition of serfdom — an audacious bid by ordinary people for a fairer society.

tech_top.headline: Trump says the only AI guardrail the US needs is him
tech_top.pm_note: The White House is signaling it won't back federal AI safety rules, so any guardrails a PM ships will be self-imposed or state-level for now.
tech_top.blurb: Trump rejected calls for AI regulation and criticized Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend essay urging the industry to slow down, saying 'a strong and smart president' is the only guardrail AI needs. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk had both voiced support for Amodei's call to pace development.

tech_top.headline: Cops searched Flock's surveillance cameras and typed 'LMAO' as the reason
tech_top.pm_note: A mandatory 'reason' field is only as good as the audit process behind it — a lesson for anyone building compliance logging into a surveillance or data-access product.
tech_top.blurb: An EFF review of Flock license-plate-reader searches found police typing 'LMAO,' 'idk,' 'asdfg' and slurs into the system's mandatory reason field while querying networks spanning thousands of cameras and hundreds of cities. Flock changed how the reason box works in late 2025, but the searches reviewed span 2023 through then.

tech_top.headline: Waymo opens robotaxi rides in Las Vegas, its 15th city
tech_top.pm_note: A 100,000-name waitlist for a market Waymo hasn't marketed shows demand has outrun the fleet — a supply problem, not a demand one.
tech_top.blurb: Waymo opened driverless rides to the public in Las Vegas, its 15th US market, with a waitlist already past 100,000 sign-ups. The initial zone covers the Strip and major resorts, running dozens of its new Ojai minivans under a Nevada permit for up to 1,000 vehicles.

tech_101.text: The idea, pushed by Anthropic's Dario Amodei, that AI labs should deliberately slow model releases to leave time for safety testing — a voluntary brake, not a law, and one Trump just said the US doesn't need.
Cameras like Flock's that log every passing license plate into a searchable, shared database. Police are supposed to record why they searched it; this week showed how loosely that gets enforced.

science.headline: A new catalyst makes 'heavy' deuterated drugs far easier to build
science.blurb: French chemists developed a nickel-catalyzed method to precisely swap hydrogen for deuterium in existing drug molecules, rather than resynthesizing them from scratch. Deuterium's heavier mass slows the enzymatic reactions that break drugs down, potentially making treatments longer-lasting with fewer doses.

science.headline: Solar Orbiter just gave scientists their sharpest look yet at the Sun's magnetic seam
science.blurb: Solar Orbiter crossed the heliospheric current sheet — the vast, rippling boundary between the Sun's magnetic hemispheres — at just a third of Earth's distance from the Sun, closer than Mercury. The pass gave researchers their most detailed composition data yet on a structure that shapes the whole solar system's magnetic field.

science.headline: A wearable sensor found the hidden hormone surges routine blood pressure tests miss
science.blurb: Continuous monitoring with a wearable device revealed nighttime aldosterone surges in patients with treatment-resistant high blood pressure, a pattern standard daytime blood tests miss entirely. The finding points to primary aldosteronism as a frequently undiagnosed cause of hypertension, and to a better way of catching it.

philosophy.headline: Philosophy has a trick for decisions where every option is defensible
philosophy.blurb: Philosopher Ruth Chang's work on 'hard choices' argues that the hardest decisions aren't between a clearly better and worse option, but between options that are genuinely on a par. Chang suggests treating the choice as an occasion to decide who you want to be, rather than searching for a hidden right answer.

philosophy.headline: Two people can look at the same evidence and reasonably live in different realities
philosophy.blurb: Sociologist Steve Fuller argues that developments across neuroscience, quantum physics and AI undermine the assumption of one shared, observer-independent reality that people merely interpret differently. If he's right, some of today's fiercest disagreements aren't about values alone — they're about which reality each side takes as given.

philosophy_101.text: Philosopher Ruth Chang's term for decisions between options that are genuinely comparable in value but not equal — neither better nor worse, just different — so no amount of information resolves them.

The view that there's no single 'view from nowhere' — that what counts as real or true is inseparable from a particular standpoint. Nietzsche's version was about values; Fuller's is aimed at physics and AI.
